nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used GAMLSS (generalized additive models for location, scale and shape) with a generalized gamma distribution, modeling age with fractional polynomials (up to 3rd order), and including study-specific random effects for mean (mu) and variance (sigma) components. The model was sex-stratified and controlled for FreeSurfer processing version.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We created brain charts for the human lifespan using generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS), a robust and flexible framework for modelling non-linear growth trajectories recommended by the World Health Organization.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Mapping normative brain growth section

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Primary phenotypes: Four cerebrum tissue volumes (total cortical grey matter volume [GMV], total white matter volume [WMV], total subcortical grey matter volume [sGMV], and total ventricular cerebrospinal fluid volume [CSF/ventricles]). Extended phenotypes: total cerebrum volume (TCV), mean cortical thickness (CT), total surface area (SA), and regional cortical volumes for 34 bilateral Desikan-Killiany parcellated regions.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: GAMLSS models were fitted to structural MRI data from control subjects for the four main tissue volumes of the cerebrum (total cortical grey matter volume (GMV), total white matter volume (WMV), total subcortical grey matter volume (sGMV) and total ventricular cerebrospinal fluid volume (ventricles or CSF)).
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Mapping normative brain growth section; Extended neuroimaging phenotypes section

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was modeled using fractional polynomials (up to 3rd order for mu component, 2nd-3rd order for sigma component) which include non-integer powers from the standard set {-2, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3}. Sex was included as a fixed effect for stratification. Study/site was modeled as a random effect on mu and sigma components. FreeSurfer preprocessing software version (five categories) was included as a fixed effect.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: For each component of the generalized gamma distribution, α terms correspond to fixed effects of the intercept, sex (female or male), and software version used for pre-processing (five categories); β terms correspond to the fixed effects of age, modelled as fractional polynomial functions with the number of terms reflecting the order of the fractional polynomials; and γ terms correspond to the study-level random effects.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Methods / Model generation and specification section
